title: Manual typewriter
prompt: A labelled teaching cutaway of the 1998 manual typewriter on pages 26 and 27 holds paper against a platen with an ink ribbon in front. Type presses one key and follows linked levers to swing a type bar and strike a lower-case letter through the ribbon. Shift and type lowers the type-bar assembly as the page 26 caption describes, aligning upper-case type with the printing point before striking. Release returns key, links and type bar to rest. Show key, connecting levers and pivots, type bar, two type faces, ribbon, paper and platen. This is a key-action cutaway. Do not claim a complete source-proved escapement, ribbon-feed or carriage-return mechanism.
blurb: A teaching key-action cutaway uses linked levers to strike inked type against paper and lowers the type-bar assembly for capitals.
chapter: Part 1: The Mechanics of Movement / Levers

identity.note: 1998 Levers / Manual typewriter. Heading and lever-chain explanation on page 27. Type-bar, case-shift, platen and ribbon captions on page 26. Small key travel becomes long type-bar travel through linked levers.
identity.classificationNote: A named machine or diagram inside Levers is not a separate main chapter. The parking-meter heading is historical.

adaptationDecision.reason: The book explicitly compares it with piano action. Existing piano-action transmits key travel to a string hammer with jack and repetition action. Typewriter transmits it to printing type and ribbon. Do not copy piano escapement parts into this apparatus.

prompt.note: Type is supported. The illustrated case shift lowers type bars for upper case, contrary to lifts in the prompt. The inspected passage does not explain a full carriage return, line feed or escapement. Use a source-bounded key-action cutaway.
prompt.apparatusRelation: Bench or scale teaching adaptation of a named book example. Controls, fixtures and test specimens stage the lesson and are not claimed as the book apparatus.

1998.inspection: Listed mechanism pages read in saved primary OCR.

2016.inspection: Inspected pages 26 and 27 discuss piano action and pedals rather than typewriter construction. No claim of absence elsewhere in 2016.

truthNotes: Source-bounded schematic of one key action, not a complete typewriter.
Five levers and fixed-length links are teaching geometry, not a measured reconstruction of the book drawing.
A translating fixture lowers the complete isolated action, including the type-bar assembly, six model units before upper-case impact. The original shift linkage is not reconstructed.
Board, supports, protective action shroud, ribbon clips and stationary paper are teaching fixtures.
The ribbon, paper and platen remain stationary. Repeated strikes overprint one point. No carriage, escapement, ribbon feed, carriage return or line feed is claimed.
1988 is access restricted and unverified. 2016 typewriter mechanism is not individually verified. No edition union is claimed.

telemetry.reason: Standalone static figure has no production telemetry. Local verification only; live verification untested.
